newsitem.title: USA: Amerijet adds Dominican Republic flights.
newsitem.headline: Amerijet adds Dominican Republic flights.

text.p: Amerijet International Inc., the Fort Lauderdale all-cargo carrier has expanded its scheduled cargo service between Miami and the Dominican Republic, a company executive told Reuters on Wednesday.
"We started service in September and business has been great," Pam Rollins, vice president, said.
"In December we were flying more than 80 flights per week and in late February we added two flights" to bring regular flights to seven," Rollins said.
Amerijet flies tobacco and other products from the Dominican Republic and flies in general cargo, Rollins said.

Privately-held Amerijet offers five flights per week to Santo Domingo and two to Puerto Plata. Amerijet serves other destinations in the Caribbean and said it can route flights based on customer demand for inter-island service.
Amerijet flies to 27 international destinations and runs at least 30 scheduled flights per week with its fleet of Boeing 727 aircraft.
